newsitem.title: UK: Clarke "probably" favours EMU if pros exceed cons.
newsitem.headline: Clarke "probably" favours EMU if pros exceed cons.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said he would probably favour Britain joining a single European currency if the advantages outweighed the disadvantages. "If those possible advantages, which I described, strongly outweigh the possible disadvantages that I described, then I would probably be in favour of joining," he told parliament.
Clarke said it was far too soon to determine where the balance of advantage for the City and British business generally lay and he believed the decision could go in either direction.
There were far too many uncertainties about the shape of the euro zone and how it would function and no-one could say when or even if it was going to happen.
"We would be very foolish to ignore the huge political capital and practical effort that is being invested in this project by the other member states of the European Union," Clarke said.
Britain had played a critical role in the design of monetary union and it was important that it continued to exert a key influence, Clarke added.
